blocks.text: Label, Ordinal, One-Hot, and Binary Encoding all shared a genuine common thread, converting or restructuring the category column itself into new integer or binary values, or into entirely new columns. Frequency encoding breaks from that pattern completely, replacing each category with a genuinely different kind of number entirely, how often that category actually appears in the data.

This topic covers exactly how frequency encoding computes and applies that proportion, why it genuinely requires no new columns at all, unlike every technique covered so far in this module, a real collision risk when two different categories happen to share the same frequency, why a category own rarity or commonness can itself carry genuine signal, and why this technique, unlike several still to come, never touches the target column at all.
1. How Frequency Encoding Actually Works
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443142920-586344242.png

Frequency encoding counts how often each genuine category appears across the dataset, converts that count into a proportion of the whole, and replaces every occurrence of that category with its own genuine proportion value. A category appearing in 150 out of 1000 rows becomes 0.15, replacing every single instance of that category directly.
This is a genuinely simple, three step process, count, convert to a proportion, replace, and it produces a single numeric column with no restructuring of the dataset shape at all.
2. No New Columns at All
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443275589-871902591.png

Every technique covered so far in this module that avoided the false ordering problem did so by adding new columns, one-hot encoding added one column per category, binary encoding added a smaller but still genuinely new set of columns. Frequency encoding genuinely needs none of that, the original single column simply has its values replaced, with the dataset shape staying exactly the same as before.

This is a genuinely real, practical advantage in high cardinality situations, frequency encoding sidesteps the entire column count problem that motivated binary encoding in the previous topic, without needing any of that extra structural complexity at all.

blocks.text: 3. A Worked Example
Computing frequency encoding directly with pandas shows this simple replacement in action, on a small column of city names.

code.content:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "city": ["mumbai", "delhi", "mumbai", "bangalore", "mumbai", "delhi"],
})

freq_map = df["city"].value_counts(normalize=True)
df["city_freq"] = df["city"].map(freq_map)

print(df)

blocks.text: mumbai, appearing 3 times out of 6 rows, genuinely becomes 0.5, while delhi, appearing twice, genuinely becomes about 0.33, and bangalore, appearing once, genuinely becomes about 0.17, each value directly reflecting how common that city actually is in this data.
4. A Real Collision Risk
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443275591-458203247.png

If two genuinely different categories happen to appear the same number of times, category A and category B both appearing in exactly 15 percent of rows, for instance, they both genuinely receive the identical frequency value, 0.15. A model can no longer genuinely distinguish between them at all, they have effectively become the same feature value, despite representing two entirely different, real categories.

This is a genuinely real risk worth being aware of, especially with a column that has many categories of similar rarity, where several genuinely distinct categories could plausibly collide into the same encoded value purely by coincidence.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Frequency encoding genuinely sacrifices category identity for compactness. Two categories with coincidentally similar frequencies become indistinguishable, a real tradeoff worth considering against the alternatives covered elsewhere in this module.

blocks.text: 5. Rarity Itself Can Be a Genuine Signal

blocks.alt: Rarity Itself Can Be a Genuine Signal
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443275591-668260933.png

Beyond simply compressing a category into a number, frequency encoding can genuinely carry real, useful signal of its own, how common or rare a category is might itself correlate with the outcome being predicted. A genuinely rare product category might see different purchase behavior than a genuinely common one, independent of anything else about that specific category.

This is a genuinely real, distinct advantage over an arbitrary label encoding, the numeric value assigned here is not random, it directly, meaningfully reflects something real and potentially useful about that category standing in the dataset.
6. Frequency Encoding Never Touches the Target

blocks.alt: Frequency Encoding Never Touches the Target
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443275592-302238175.png

It is genuinely worth being explicit about what frequency encoding does and does not use, it computes its values entirely from the feature column itself, how often each category appears, and never looks at the target column at all. This is a genuinely important distinction from Target Encoding and Mean Encoding, covered later in this module, both of which deliberately do use target information, and carry a genuine leakage risk as a direct consequence.

Frequency encoding, by contrast, genuinely carries no target leakage risk of that specific kind, since the target is never consulted anywhere in its computation, a real, meaningful safety advantage worth remembering when comparing it against those later techniques.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: When choosing between frequency encoding and the target based techniques covered later in this module, start with frequency encoding whenever a simpler, genuinely leakage-free option is acceptable for the problem at hand.

blocks.text: 7. A Subtler Leakage Consideration Still Applies

blocks.alt: A Subtler Leakage Consideration Still Applies
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443275592-883507135.png

Even though frequency encoding genuinely never touches the target, a subtler version of the leakage discipline from earlier in this course still genuinely applies, category frequencies should be computed from the training set only, then applied unchanged to validation and test, exactly the same discipline covered for scalers in the previous module and for label encoders earlier in this one.

Computing frequencies from the full dataset before splitting would genuinely let the validation and test set own category distributions quietly influence the encoding applied to training data, a genuine, if more subtle, instance of the train test contamination covered back in Data Leakage.
8. Frequency Encoding Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Frequency Encoding Versus What Comes Next
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785443275592-42120295.png

Frequency encoding introduced a genuinely different strategy, deriving a meaningful number directly from the feature itself rather than restructuring it into new columns. The next topic takes this genuine same core idea and applies one small, specific variation to it.

Count Encoding, covered next, uses the genuine same underlying approach, but works with raw counts directly instead of normalized proportions, a small but genuinely meaningful difference worth understanding clearly.

items: Frequency encoding replaces each category with the proportion of rows that genuinely share that category.
It requires no new columns at all, unlike one-hot or binary encoding covered earlier in this module.
Two categories with a genuinely coincidentally similar frequency become indistinguishable to a model.
A category own rarity or commonness can itself carry genuine, useful predictive signal.
Frequency encoding never touches the target column, unlike target and mean encoding covered later in this module.
Frequencies must still genuinely be computed only from the training set, respecting the same leakage discipline as always.
